explanation: Sher Shah Suri, who briefly ruled northern India, issued a silver coin called the rupiya in the 1540s, ancestor of the rupee. The US Mint struck its first silver dollars in 1794.

claims.text: Sher Shah Suri issued a silver coin called the rupiya during his rule over northern India, from 1540 to 1545.
The US Mint struck its first silver dollar coins in 1794.
The modern rupee takes its name from Sher Shah Suri's rupiya.
